                "Topic": "B.012 expected value decision planning",
                "MicroTopic": "expected value decision planning",
                "UniqueConceptKey": "B-012-expected-value-decision-planning",
                "LOSTag": "B.3 Forecasting techniques",
                "Difficulty": "Moderate-Easy",
                "ItemType": "MCQ",
                "ItemStyle": "single-select",
                "Stem": "Delta has several demand scenarios with probabilities. Which response is most appropriate?",
                "Choices": {
                        "A": "Select only the best-case outcome because it is possible",
                        "B": "Record the expected value as guaranteed revenue",
                        "C": "Ignore probabilities and use the most recent actual outcome",
                        "D": "Compute the probability-weighted average outcome to support planning under uncertainty"
                },
                "CorrectChoice": "D",
                "ExplanationCorrect": "Expected value weights outcomes by their probabilities; it is a planning tool, not a guaranteed result.",
                "StudyLinks": [
                        {
                                "label": "IMA CMA Learning Outcome Statements, Part 1 Section B",
                                "url": "https://prodcm.imanet.org/-/media/IMA/Files/Home/IMA-Certifications/CMA-Certification/2024-CMA-Learning-Outcome-Statement-Final.ashx"
                        },
                        {
                                "label": "OpenStax Managerial Accounting: Budgeting",
                                "url": "https://openstax.org/books/principles-managerial-accounting/pages/7-introduction"
                        }
                ],
                "SourceDescription": "Original CMA Part 1 exam-style practice. Not real CMA exam content and not copied from official samples.",
                "Part1OnlyFlag": true,
                "ReviewNote": "If missed or marked, review the linked study materials and rework the underlying concept without looking at the answer.",
                "QuestionID": "P1-B-012",
                "CalculationItem": false,
                "VerifiedChecks": [
                        "Mapped to CMA Part 1 Learning Outcome Statements effective September 1, 2024",
                        "Screened to exclude Part 2-only topics such as CVP, financial ratio analysis, capital budgeting, corporate finance, ERM, and ethics",
                        "Original practice item with unique micro-topic and stem",
                        "Answer key distribution balanced across A/B/C/D",
                        "Distractors written as plausible CMA-style traps"
                ],
                "ExplanationWrongA": "Selecting only the best-case outcome ignores probability — planning under uncertainty requires considering all possible outcomes weighted by their likelihood. The best case may have a very low probability, and basing plans solely on it exposes the organization to significant downside risk from more likely but less favorable scenarios.",
                "ExplanationWrongB": "Expected value is a planning tool, not a revenue recognition basis. It represents the probability-weighted average across multiple scenarios — none of which may actually occur. Recording expected value as guaranteed revenue would overstate income and violate the revenue recognition principle, which requires performance obligations to be satisfied before revenue is recorded.",
                "ExplanationWrongC": "Ignoring probabilities and relying on the most recent actual outcome discards all forward-looking information embedded in the demand scenarios. Expected value analysis explicitly incorporates probability assessments to produce a weighted-average outcome, providing a more complete basis for planning under uncertainty than a single historical data point.",
